Hannah / team — responding to Emily's items with a suggested concession package that should keep margin intact and address Greenline's operational asks. Proposed updates to present in the final doc: 

- True-up cadence: offer monthly true-ups for Growth if Greenline commits to a 12-month prepay slab or a slightly higher effective rate (we can use $0.000096 token vs $0.000095 listed) — this helps cashflow and forecasting for them and preserves our exposure.
- Carry-forward mechanics: show as an invoice balance labeled "Committed Credit (CFQ)" that reduces next invoice; up to 20% allowed per quarter in year 1. Any carry-forward balance not consumed by year-end converts to a one-time ledger credit at 60% of list on-demand rate (we avoid refunding cash).
- Pilot ramp example (Growth at 50% usage month 1–3):
  * Commit: 250M/yr => monthly commitment ~20.8M tokens.
  * Month 1 usage at 50% => 10.4M tokens charged at blended pilot rate: we propose applying 60-day ramp credit ($10k) first, then invoice the remainder at on-commit rate. Effective per-token for months 1–3 (after $10k credit) ~ $0.00011 token (conservative example).
- Dedicated capacity credit: allow conversion of up to 5% of annual commit into Dedicated Capacity credits (non-transferable, one-time allocation) if SLA breach and mutually agreed capacity need arises. This must be explicitly invoked in the SLA appendix.

Attachments: 20261119_greenline_mutual_action_plan.xlsx (MOP + timeline + sign-off owners).

If legal signs off on the carry-forward wording we can move this to a final PDF w/ DocuSign. Marissa — loop with procurement counsel? Karthik — FYI for data residency clause in Enterprise section.

— Ben
